findings.observation: A large window brings strong daylight into the sleeping area.
The bed has a solid headboard against a wall, giving supported rest.

findings.principle: Bed in Line with the Door
findings.observation: The foot of the bed points straight at the open door — the classic 'coffin position' that drains restful energy.
A wall mirror directly faces the bed, bouncing active energy at sleepers.
Boxes stored under the bed block chi from circulating beneath the sleeper.
An exposed beam crosses above the bed, pressing down on the sleeping area.

suggestions.title: Shift the bed off the door line
suggestions.detail: Slide the bed so the foot no longer aims at the doorway while keeping a view of the door.

suggestions.title: Reposition or cover the mirror
suggestions.detail: Angle the mirror away from the bed or drape it at night.

suggestions.title: Clear under the bed
suggestions.detail: Move the boxes to a closet so air and energy can flow beneath you.

findings.observation: A healthy plant adds wood energy and life to the room.
The window corner brings generous daylight into the seating area.
The sofa sits across the walkway from the door, interrupting the natural flow through the room.

findings.principle: Heavy Mass in the Light Corner
findings.observation: A tall, heavy bookcase occupies the brightest corner, weighing down its uplifting energy.
Boxes and piles gather in the center of the room, stagnating energy.

suggestions.title: Open the entry path
suggestions.detail: Rotate the sofa to run parallel with the walkway so the route from the door flows freely.

suggestions.title: Swap the bookcase and plant
suggestions.detail: Move the bookcase to a dimmer wall and let the plant take the bright corner.

suggestions.title: Clear the floor piles
suggestions.detail: Basket or shelve the loose items to restore open floor.

findings.observation: Herb plants on the floor add living wood energy to balance the fire of the stove.
A window keeps the cooking area bright and airy.
The stove and sink sit directly adjacent, placing fire and water elements in conflict.
A knife block sits in open view, projecting sharp energy across the counter.

suggestions.title: Buffer stove and sink
suggestions.detail: Place a small wooden cutting board or a potted herb between the stove and sink to mediate fire and water.

suggestions.title: Store knives in a drawer
suggestions.detail: Move the knife block into a drawer with an in-drawer organizer.

findings.observation: Fixtures are grouped tidily along one wall, keeping the water zone contained.
A clean mirror above the sink expands light in a small space.
The toilet lid is up — in Feng Shui terms, wealth energy literally drains away.
No natural light leaves the room's energy heavy and damp.

suggestions.title: Keep the lid down
suggestions.detail: Close the toilet lid (and the door) to stop the symbolic drain.

suggestions.title: Warm the light
suggestions.detail: Add warm-white bulbs and a small plant that tolerates low light (pothos) to lift the energy.

findings.observation: The window gives the work area steady daylight.
A plant near the desk adds growth energy to the work zone.
The desk chair faces away from the door — outside the commanding position, inviting unease.
Loose cables tangle beneath the desk, snarling the flow of the workspace.

suggestions.title: Turn the desk to command the room
suggestions.detail: Rotate the desk so you face the door with the wall at your back.

suggestions.title: Tame the cables
suggestions.detail: Bundle cables into a sleeve or under-desk tray.

findings.observation: The room reads open and usable, with furniture scaled to the space.
Daylight reaches the main area of the room.
Materials and colors lean on one or two elements, leaving the palette slightly unbalanced.

suggestions.title: Round out the elements
suggestions.detail: Add an accent in an underrepresented element — a plant (wood), warm lamp (fire), or ceramic piece (earth).

suggestions.title: Keep pathways clear
suggestions.detail: Maintain an open route from the door through the room.
